intent_routes.question: Where is ATIS required?

Which countries require ATIS?
intent_routes.answer: ATIS is required for vessels making VHF transmissions on inland waterways of RAINWAT signatory countries, including Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Hungary, Luxembourg, Moldova, Montenegro, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovak Republic, and Switzerland

intent_routes.question: What is an MMSI number?
question_variations: How do I get an MMSI?
Can I change my MMSI?
intent_routes.answer: An MMSI (Marine Mobile Service Identity) is a unique nine digit number used on marine transceivers with DSC capability. It must be assigned by an approved authority and cannot be self-assigned. Once entered into the radio, it cannot be changed without returning to a dealer

intent_routes.question: What is an ATIS ID?
question_variations: Do I need an ATIS ID?
How is ATIS ID different from MMSI?
intent_routes.answer: An ATIS ID is required in certain EU countries when navigating inland waterways. It is usually different from your MMSI and must be assigned by an approved authority

intent_routes.question: How reliable is AIS for navigation?
question_variations: Can I rely on AIS alone?
What are AIS limitations?
intent_routes.answer: AIS should not be relied upon as the sole navigation aid. It is only an aid to navigation and not a replacement for vigilant human lookouts and other navigation aids such as RADAR. Not all vessels have AIS installed or turned on, and performance can be impaired by installation issues or environmental factors

intent_routes.question: What handsets are compatible with the RS100/V100 system?

What types of handsets can I use with V100?
How many handsets can connect to RS100?
intent_routes.answer: The system supports up to 4 wired alphanumeric handset stations (HS100/H100) and up to 4 wireless handsets (HS40/H60)

intent_routes.question: What are the main features of the RS100-B/V100-B AIS system?
question_variations: What AIS capabilities does RS100-B have?
How does AIS work on V100-B?
What's special about the B version AIS features?
intent_routes.answer: The B version includes an AIS dual channel receiver to receive and display AIS targets, and an AIS Class-B Transmitter to transmit vessel position and details. This requires an additional VHF antenna installation.

intent_routes.question: How many speaker outputs does the system have?
question_variations: What's the speaker configuration?

What are the speaker specifications?
intent_routes.answer: The system has 4 configurable 4W wired speaker outputs

intent_routes.question: What safety features are included in the system?
question_variations: What emergency functions does it have?
How does the distress call work?
What are the emergency capabilities?
intent_routes.answer: Safety features include DSC capability meeting Global DSC Class D Standards, DISTRESS call key for automatic MMSI and position transmission, Man Over Board (MOB) function, and dedicated CH16/9 key for quick access to the international distress channel

intent_routes.question: How many contacts can be stored in the system?
question_variations: What's the contact storage capacity?
How many MMSI numbers can I save?
What's the contact list limit?
intent_routes.answer: The system can store up to 50 contacts with MMSI numbers and up to 20 groups with MMSI numbers

intent_routes.question: How many contacts can be stored in the contacts list?

intent_routes.question: What are the transmission power options?

Can I adjust transmission power?
intent_routes.answer: There are two transmission power options: High (25 W) or Low (1 W)

intent_routes.question: How do I enter text or numbers?

How do I input text?
intent_routes.answer: Use the up/down keys to scroll through alphanumeric characters, or use the keypad on the wired handset (press key multiple times for different letters). Press OK/HL to select and move to next character. Press DSC/MENU to go back, or X/POWER to cancel entry.

intent_routes.question: What additional features does the B model provide?

What capabilities does the B model add?

intent_routes.question: How do I navigate the menus?
question_variations: What are the menu navigation controls?
How do I move through menu options?
intent_routes.answer: Press X/POWER key to step back or exit menus. Press OK/HL key to make selections. Use scroll bar to see additional options above or below displayed menu text. Selected menu items are highlighted.
references: How to display and navigate menus section

intent_routes.question: How do I make a distress call?
question_variations: How do I send an emergency signal?
What is the procedure for distress calls?
How do I activate the distress button?
intent_routes.answer: There are two ways: Short press the Distress button to make a call where you can select the nature of distress from a list. Long press the Distress button to immediately send an 'undesignated' distress call. The call will broadcast to all DSC radios in range and include position if available.

intent_routes.question: What does the AIS indicator mean?
question_variations: How do I know if AIS is working?
What are the AIS status indicators?
intent_routes.answer: The AIS indicator shows three possible states for NRS-2 models: AIS function enabled (Receive only mode), AIS Class-B enabled (Transmit and Receive mode), or AIS Class-B Silent Switch mode (transmissions disabled)

intent_routes.question: How do I switch to Channel 16?
question_variations: What is the quick way to access Channel 16?
How do I get to the emergency channel?
intent_routes.answer: Short press the 16/9 button to change to Channel 16. Press again to return to the original channel.

intent_routes.question: When does the low battery warning activate?
question_variations: At what voltage does low battery warning show?
What triggers the low battery alert?
intent_routes.answer: The low battery (vessel) warning activates when voltage drops to 10.5V

intent_routes.question: Where is the GPS status shown?
question_variations: How do I check GPS status?
What indicates GPS is working?
intent_routes.answer: GPS status is shown by indicator H on the LCD display. It shows whether Internal or External GPS is enabled and if there is a valid 3D fix

intent_routes.question: How do I turn on the radio system?
question_variations: How to power on the radio?
What's the procedure to start the radio system?
Can I turn on the radio from any handset?
intent_routes.answer: The radio system can only be turned ON from a Fixed Handset (F1-F4) by long pressing the X/POWER key

intent_routes.question: How do I transmit on the radio?
question_variations: What button do I press to talk?
How do I use PTT?
How can I broadcast a message?
intent_routes.answer: Press and hold the PTT (Push-to-talk) key to transmit. Only hold it down for the duration of your message. Note that the radio cannot receive while PTT is pressed.

intent_routes.question: How do I change channels?
question_variations: What's the way to switch channels?
Can I directly select a channel?
How to navigate between channels?
intent_routes.answer: You can change channels in three ways: 1) Short press Channel UP/DOWN keys to increase/decrease one channel at a time 2) Long press Channel UP/DOWN to rapidly scroll through channels 3) Directly type the channel number on the keypad

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the transmission power?
question_variations: How to switch between high and low power?
What's the process to change transmission power?
How do I toggle between 25W and 1W?
intent_routes.answer: Long press the OK/HL key to toggle between HIGH (25W) and LOW (1W) power for the entire channel bank. The selection will be displayed as HI or LO on the LCD. Note that some channels only allow low power transmissions.

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust volume and squelch?
question_variations: What's the process to change volume?
How can I control the squelch?
How do I use the VOL/SQL controls?
intent_routes.answer: Short press the VOL/SQL Selector to toggle between Volume and Squelch control. A triangular arrow above the level bar indicates which is selected. Use the + and - keys to adjust the selected control.

intent_routes.question: How do I enter Intercom mode?
question_variations: How to access the intercom?
How do I use the intercom feature?
What button activates intercom mode?
intent_routes.answer: Long press the Intercom/Hailer/Fog Horn/Announce button to enter Intercom mode

intent_routes.question: How do I access weather stations in US/Canada mode?
question_variations: How to get NOAA weather?
How do I hear weather stations?
What button is for weather information?
intent_routes.answer: Short press the Weather button to hear the most recently selected NOAA/Canadian weather station (US/CAN country mode only)

intent_routes.question: What are the AIS plotter zoom ranges?
question_variations: What zoom levels are available for AIS?
How far can I zoom on AIS plotter?
What are the AIS scale options?
intent_routes.answer: The AIS plotter has 6 zoom ranges: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 nautical miles

intent_routes.question: How do I activate Man Over Board (MOB)?
question_variations: What is the MOB button combination?
How to mark MOB position?
What triggers MOB waypoint?
intent_routes.answer: Long press both SCAN and TRI keys simultaneously to mark the current location with a Man-Over-Board (MOB) waypoint

intent_routes.question: How do I replay recent radio traffic?
question_variations: How to access voice recording?
Can I playback recent transmissions?
How do I hear previous radio calls?
intent_routes.answer: Short press the Voice Recorder Playback button to replay the last 60 seconds of VHF radio traffic

intent_routes.question: How do the numeric keys work in different modes?
question_variations: What do the number buttons do?
How do numeric keys function?
What are the keypad functions?
intent_routes.answer: In NORMAL mode: short press enters digits, long press opens functions. In DATA INPUT mode: enters numbers and letters. In INTERCOM mode: makes direct calls to other stations

intent_routes.question: How do I make a direct call to another intercom station?
question_variations: How can I call another intercom station?
What button do I press for intercom calls?
How do intercom direct calls work?
intent_routes.answer: In Intercom mode, press the number key (1-8) corresponding to the handset you want to call. For example, press 1 for Handset-1, press 2 for Handset-2, etc.

intent_routes.question: What does pressing key 0 do in different modes?
question_variations: How does the 0 key function?
What are the functions of zero key?
What happens when I press 0?
intent_routes.answer: Key 0 has different functions depending on mode: In Normal mode it inputs 0, in Data input mode it inputs 0 or space (long press), in Intercom mode it calls all IC stations (short press) or triggers All PA announce tone (long press)

intent_routes.question: How do I access the Hailer mode menu?
question_variations: Where is the Hailer mode setting?
What button activates Hailer mode?
How to enter Hailer mode?
intent_routes.answer: Long press the 0 key in Normal mode to access the Hailer mode menu

intent_routes.question: What are the different operating modes available?
question_variations: Which modes can the system operate in?
What modes does the system have?
List all operating modes
intent_routes.answer: The system has three main operating modes: Normal mode, Data input mode, and Intercom mode. Each mode provides different functions for the keypad.

intent_routes.question: How do I enter letters during data input?
question_variations: How can I type letters?
What keys do I use for alphabetic input?
How to input text characters?
intent_routes.answer: In Data input mode, keys 2-9 can input letters: 2(ABC), 3(DEF), 4(GHI), 5(JKL), 6(MNO), 7(PQRS), 8(TUV), 9(WXYZ). The displayed letter is accepted after a short pause or pressing a different key.

intent_routes.question: How do I open the main menu on the radio?
question_variations: What button opens the menu?
How to access the main menu?
Where is the menu button?
intent_routes.answer: Long press the DSC/MENU key to open the main Menu page

intent_routes.question: What are the available scan options?
question_variations: What types of scan can I do?
How many scan modes are there?
What scanning features are available?
intent_routes.answer: Available scan options are: ALL SCAN, ALL CHANNELS + 16, MY CHANNELS, MY CHANNELS + 16, and EDIT MY CHANNELS

intent_routes.question: What watch modes are available?
question_variations: What are the watch features?
How many watch modes exist?
What watch options do I have?
intent_routes.answer: Available watch modes are: DUAL WATCH, TRI WATCH, and SET WATCH with choosable channel

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the display settings?
question_variations: Where are the display controls?
How can I change screen settings?
What display options are available?
intent_routes.answer: Display settings include: TIME DISPLAY (ON/OFF), POS DISPLAY (ON/OFF), COG/SOG (ON/OFF), BACKLIGHT LEVEL, BACKLIGHT NETWORK CONFIG, and CONTRAST (0-10)

intent_routes.question: What are the radio setup options?
question_variations: How do I configure radio settings?
What can I adjust in radio setup?
Where are the radio configuration options?
intent_routes.answer: Radio setup options include: UIC (USA/INT'L/CANADA), Power Output (HIGH/LOW), CH Name, Key Beep (0-10), Units, Handset Speaker (ON/OFF), External Speaker, GPS, COM Port, Time, Vessel Call Sign, and Auto Power On settings

intent_routes.question: How do watch modes work on the radio?
question_variations: What are watch modes?
How does channel scanning work?
Can you explain watch modes?
intent_routes.answer: Watch modes scan selected channels every 3 seconds to check for active radio communication. They are not available when ATIS mode is on.

intent_routes.question: What is the difference between Dual Watch and Tri Watch?
question_variations: How do Dual Watch and Tri Watch compare?
Should I use Dual or Tri Watch?
intent_routes.answer: Dual Watch monitors the current channel and priority channel. Tri Watch monitors the current channel, priority channel, and a user-selected watch channel.

intent_routes.question: How does the voice recorder function work?
question_variations: Can I record radio communications?
What is the voice recorder feature?
intent_routes.answer: The voice recorder can record the last 60 seconds of transmitted and received VHF audio in a loop when turned ON. Playback options include 15-second forward and rewind functions.

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the backlight?
question_variations: Can I change the screen brightness?
Where is the backlight setting?
intent_routes.answer: Backlight can be adjusted from level 1-10 using the up/down keys. Press DSC/MENU key to activate night mode. The setting can be synchronized with other network devices through Network Config settings.

intent_routes.question: What is the difference between LOCAL and DISTANT sensitivity settings?
question_variations: When should I use LOCAL vs DISTANT mode?
How do sensitivity settings work?
intent_routes.answer: LOCAL mode is designed for areas with high radio noise like ports or cities. DISTANT mode is better for open sea conditions and improves receiver sensitivity over distances.

intent_routes.question: How do I start scanning all channels?
question_variations: How to scan channels?
Can I scan all frequencies?
What is the all scan function?
intent_routes.answer: Press the SCAN key to access scan menu, then select All Scan. This will scan all channels cyclically. When a signal is received, scanning stops at that channel. Scanning resumes after 5 seconds of silence.

intent_routes.question: What is Dual Watch mode?
question_variations: How does dual watch work?
Can I monitor two channels?
What does dual watch do?
intent_routes.answer: Dual Watch allows you to monitor the current channel and the priority channel simultaneously. The radio checks both channels every 3 seconds for active communication.

intent_routes.question: How do I skip a channel during scanning?
question_variations: Can I skip busy channels?
How to lock out channels from scan?
What is channel skip function?
intent_routes.answer: Press OK when stopped on a busy channel to permanently skip it. The SKIP icon will appear for that channel. To cancel a skip, select the channel in normal mode and press OK again.

intent_routes.question: What scan options are available?
question_variations: What types of scan can I use?
What are the different scan modes?
How many scan options are there?
intent_routes.answer: There are 4 scan options: 1) All channels 2) All channels + 16 (priority) 3) My channels 4) My channels + 16. The +16 options check the priority channel after every channel step.

intent_routes.question: Where do I edit My Channels list?
question_variations: How do I customize channel list?
Can I create my own channel list?
How to modify My Channels?
intent_routes.answer: Access Edit My Channels through the menu or shortcut. This allows you to create a custom list of channels that will be used during My Channels scan mode.

intent_routes.question: How do I change the radio channel bank?
question_variations: How do I switch between USA and International channels?
Can I change to Canadian channels?
How to select different channel banks?
intent_routes.answer: Select between USA, INT (International) or CAN (Canadian) channel banks. The selected bank will be displayed on the LCD screen. Note that UIC is not available in EU country mode.

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the radio power output?
question_variations: Can I switch between high and low power?
How do I change transmission power?
What are the power settings available?
intent_routes.answer: Toggle between High power (25W) or Low power (1W) transmission power for the entire channel bank. High power is indicated by an icon, Low power by LO. Note that some channels are restricted to low power only.

intent_routes.question: How do I edit channel names?
question_variations: Can I customize channel descriptions?
How to change channel display names?
What's the maximum length for channel names?
intent_routes.answer: Select Channel Name function to edit the description of the currently used channel. Channel names can be maximum 12 characters long. This function is also available as a Shortcut.

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust key beep volume?
question_variations: Can I turn off key beeps?
What's the volume range for key beeps?
How to change button sound volume?
intent_routes.answer: Select Key Beeps to adjust volume from 00 to 10, where 00 is off and 10 is loudest. This function is also available as a Shortcut.

intent_routes.question: How do I configure external speakers?
question_variations: How to set up multiple speakers?
Can I adjust external speaker volume?
How do I associate speakers with handsets?
intent_routes.answer: In Speaker Config, associate External speakers with Fixed handsets. Select HANDSET column and choose handset. Adjust volume offset between -10 to +10 in OFFSET column. Press DSC/MENU to save or X/POWER to cancel.

intent_routes.question: How do I enter GPS coordinates manually?
question_variations: Can I input GPS position manually?
What happens when I enter GPS manually?
How to set GPS position without receiver?
intent_routes.answer: Select MANUAL under GPS to enter position and time manually when not receiving GPS data. Manual positions can be used for DSC calls but not AIS. Manual positions show with 'M' prefix and are replaced when real GPS data is received.

intent_routes.question: How do I select a GPS source on my marine radio?
question_variations: Where do I set the GPS source?
How do I change GPS settings on NRS-1?
What GPS sources are available on my radio?
intent_routes.answer: For NRS-1, you can select between Networked GPS (NMEA 2000® or NMEA 0183®) or Internal GPS. For NRS-2, only Internal GPS is available. For NMEA 2000®, you can choose AUTO SELECT or pick from available network devices. For Internal GPS, a GPS-500 Antenna must be connected to the GPS port.

intent_routes.question: What is GPS SIM mode?
question_variations: How does GPS simulator work?
Can I use GPS simulator for navigation?
What does GPS SIM do?
intent_routes.answer: GPS SIM is a demonstration mode that simulates Speed Over Ground (SOG), Course Over Ground (COG), and position data. It cannot be used for DSC transmission or AIS. The simulator turns off when power is cycled or real GPS data becomes available.

intent_routes.question: How do I set the COM port baud rate?
question_variations: What baud rate should I use?
How do I configure NMEA 0183 speed?
Which COM port settings are needed for AIS?
intent_routes.answer: Select either 38400 or 4800 BAUD. AIS typically requires 38400 baud (default setting). On NRS-2, selecting 4800 will display a 'data may be lost' warning.

intent_routes.question: How do I set the local time offset?
question_variations: How do I adjust the time zone?
Can I change the time display?
How do I set the correct time?
intent_routes.answer: Select TIME OFFSET to enter the difference between UTC and local time in 15-minute increments, up to ±13 hours maximum. Note that this does not automatically adjust for Daylight Savings Time.

intent_routes.question: What happens when manual position is entered?
question_variations: How is manual position shown?
Will GPS override manual position?
How do I know if position is manual?
intent_routes.answer: When manual position is entered, latitude and longitude are displayed with a prefix 'M'. This manual entry is automatically replaced when a real GPS position is received via NMEA 0183®, NMEA 2000® or Internal GPS.

intent_routes.question: How do I set the menu timeout on my marine radio?
question_variations: What are the menu timeout options?
Can I change the menu inactivity timeout?
How long before menu times out?
intent_routes.answer: You can set the menu timeout to NONE, 5 MINS, 10 MINS, or 15 MINS. The default setting is 10 MINS. This returns the radio to normal operational mode after period of inactivity.

intent_routes.question: What is the ATIS function used for?
question_variations: When should I enable ATIS?
Do I need ATIS enabled?
Where is ATIS required?
intent_routes.answer: ATIS must be enabled when navigating inland waterways in signatory countries of the RAINWAT agreement. It should NOT be used outside these regions. When enabled, the ATIS symbol is displayed and CH10 is automatically selected. Note that DSC functionality is disabled when ATIS is turned ON.

intent_routes.question: How does automatic channel switching work?
question_variations: What is Auto Switch Channel?
Can the radio automatically change channels?
How does AUTO SWITCH work for DSC calls?
intent_routes.answer: With AUTO SWITCH ON, the radio will automatically switch channels after a 10 second delay when receiving All Ships or Group DSC calls with channel change requests. Options are provided to switch immediately or reject the request. With AUTO SWITCH OFF, all channel change requests require manual confirmation.

intent_routes.question: What are the position acknowledgment options?
question_variations: How do I handle position requests?
Can the radio automatically send position data?
What are the settings for position requests?
intent_routes.answer: There are three options for position acknowledgment: AUTO (automatically sends current position), MANUAL (operator must choose to send position), and OFF (all position requests are ignored).

intent_routes.question: How do I enter an MMSI number?
question_variations: Where do I get an MMSI number?
Can I make up an MMSI number?
How do I change my MMSI number?
intent_routes.answer: MMSI numbers must be supplied by a local radio spectrum authority. DO NOT enter a random made-up number. Contact a Simrad® or B&G® dealer if you need to change your MMSI after initial input. An MMSI number is required before DSC function can be enabled.

intent_routes.question: How does Auto Switch Channel work on the radio?
question_variations: What happens when Auto Switch is enabled?
How does automatic channel switching work?
What is the Auto Switch feature?
intent_routes.answer: When Auto Switch is ON and an All Ships or Group DSC call is received, the radio will automatically switch channels after a 10 second delay. You'll have options to switch immediately or stay on the current channel.

intent_routes.question: What is AIS Silent Mode?
question_variations: How do I pause AIS transmissions?
Can I stop AIS transmitting?
What does Silent Mode do?
intent_routes.answer: Silent Mode pauses AIS transmissions while still receiving AIS traffic. It can be activated via the menu, from a Simrad/B&G MFD, or using a hardwired switch connected to the NRS-2 Blackbox AUX terminal.

intent_routes.question: How do I set up CPA alerts?
question_variations: What is the CPA setting?
How do I configure Closest Point of Approach?
How do CPA alarms work?
intent_routes.answer: CPA (Closest Point of Approach) can be set in 0.1 NM increments from 0.1 to 25.1 NM. The CPA ALARM must be turned ON in the ALARMS menu for alerts to work. TCPA (Time to CPA) can be set from 1-30 minutes in 30-second increments.

intent_routes.question: What are the DSC timeout options?
question_variations: How long is the DSC inactivity timeout?
What timeout settings are available for DSC?
When does DSC timeout occur?
intent_routes.answer: DSC timeouts can be set for both Distress and Non-distress calls. Options are NONE, 5 MINS, 10 MINS and 15 MINS. Default is NO TIMEOUT for Distress calls and 15 MINS for Non-distress calls.

intent_routes.question: How does automatic test acknowledgement work?
question_variations: What is test acknowledge mode?
Does the radio auto-acknowledge test calls?
How do test call acknowledgements work?
intent_routes.answer: In Auto mode, DSC test calls are automatically acknowledged after a 10 second delay. In Manual mode, the operator must manually choose to send acknowledgement or cancel.

intent_routes.question: How do I enter my ship's name in the radio?
question_variations: Where do I input vessel name?
How to set ship name in system?
intent_routes.answer: Enter the ship's name using maximum 20 alpha-numeric characters. Use the arrow keys to select the field, press OK to select, then use forward/back keys to select characters and press OK to confirm each character.

intent_routes.question: What are the vessel dimension measurements needed?
question_variations: How do I measure vessel dimensions?
What dimensions need to be entered for AIS?
intent_routes.answer: Enter four measurements in meters: A (bow to GPS antenna), B (stern to GPS antenna), C (port side to GPS antenna), and D (starboard side to GPS antenna). Note that A+B or C+D cannot equal 0.

intent_routes.question: How do I save vessel details?
question_variations: What button saves ship information?
How to store vessel data?
intent_routes.answer: Press the TRI key to save the details, then press OK again to confirm save. Alternatively, press X to exit without saving and X again to confirm exit without saving.

intent_routes.question: Can I change vessel details after saving?
question_variations: How to modify saved ship information?
Is it possible to edit vessel data after saving?
intent_routes.answer: No, each field can only be entered once. Contact a Simrad® or B&G® dealer if you need to change the vessel details after saving.

intent_routes.question: What is the GPS Alert function?
question_variations: How does GPS warning work?
What happens when GPS alert triggers?
intent_routes.answer: The GPS alert warns when the GPS source isn't outputting valid position data. It includes audible alarm, screen flash, and warning text. Can be set to OFF to disable all GPS alerts.

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust alert volume?
question_variations: Can I change alarm volume?
What are the alert sound options?
intent_routes.answer: Alert volume can be set to HIGH, LOW, or OFF for both GPS and WX alerts.

intent_routes.question: How do I turn off weather alerts on my radio?
question_variations: Can I disable weather alerts?
How to stop weather alert notifications?
Turn off WX alerts
intent_routes.answer: Set the WX Alert Function to OFF. This will disable all weather alert responses including automatic channel switching, audible alarms, screen messages, and screen flash.

intent_routes.question: What are the weather alert volume options?
question_variations: How loud can I set weather alerts?
Can I adjust alert volume?
Weather alert sound levels
intent_routes.answer: Alert volume can be set to HIGH, LOW, or OFF.

intent_routes.question: What is a SAME code?
question_variations: How does SAME coding work?
What does SAME mean in weather radio?
Explain SAME area codes
intent_routes.answer: SAME (Specific Area Message Encoding) is a digital encoding system used by NOAA Weather Radio to broadcast location-specific weather alerts. Each transmitter has a unique 6-digit code identifying geographic areas for targeted alerts.

intent_routes.question: How do I add a SAME area code?
question_variations: Setting up SAME codes
Enter new SAME code
Program SAME area code
intent_routes.answer: Select to add a SAME area code, then select NEW CODE to add a 6-digit code. At least one code must be selected for SAME to be active.

intent_routes.question: What is a T/CPA alarm?
question_variations: Explain T/CPA alerts
How does T/CPA warning work?
What does T/CPA mean?
intent_routes.answer: T/CPA alarm warns when another vessel is calculated to come within a certain distance of your vessel. It includes audible and visual alerts (screen flash and warning text) when a vessel is deemed UNSAFE based on T/CPA calculations.

intent_routes.question: How do I silence a T/CPA alert?
question_variations: Stop T/CPA alarm
Disable T/CPA warning
Cancel T/CPA alert
intent_routes.answer: Press X to silence the alert temporarily, or press DSC/Menu to Ignore further alerts from this specific vessel. Press DSC/Menu again to confirm ignore status.

intent_routes.question: How do I pair a wireless handset?
question_variations: How to connect a wireless handset?
What's the process for pairing a WHS?
How do I set up a new wireless handset?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Ensure the WHS is charged and turned OFF. Keep other WHS units OFF. 2. Access Main menu from fixed handset, select HANDSETS > WIRELESS HANDSET. 3. Select PAIR A HANDSET and YES. 4. Turn ON the wireless handset - it will show SEARCHING. 5. Press and hold SCAN key until HANDSET IS PAIRING appears.
models: All models with wireless handset support

intent_routes.question: How many handsets can the system support?
question_variations: What's the maximum number of handsets?
How many handsets can I connect?
What's the handset limit?
intent_routes.answer: The system supports up to eight handsets total: up to four fixed/wired handsets (FHS) and up to four wireless handsets (WHS).

intent_routes.question: How do I remove a wireless handset?
question_variations: How to unpair a WHS?
How do I delete a paired handset?
What's the process to remove a wireless handset?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Select REMOVE A WHS from the WIRELESS HANDSET submenu. 2. Select the handset you want to remove, press the OK key, and select YES.
models: All models with wireless handset support

intent_routes.question: How do I locate a wireless handset?
question_variations: How can I find my wireless handset?
What's the process to locate a WHS?
How do I make my wireless handset beep?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Select LOCATE A WHS from the WIRELESS HANDSET submenu. 2. Use ▲ and ▼ to select the handset. 3. Press OK. The selected handset will beep for 30 seconds if it's turned ON and within range.
models: All models with wireless handset support

intent_routes.question: What happens when I ignore a T/CPA alert?
question_variations: How long until a T/CPA alert sounds again?
Will ignored T/CPA alerts come back?
Do ignored vessels stay ignored?
intent_routes.answer: The T/CPA alert will sound again after 1 minute if the AIS alarm hasn't been resolved. Ignored vessels are reset when the radio is re-powered.

intent_routes.question: What does the DSC function test show?
question_variations: How do I check if DSC is working?
What is the DSC self-test result?
How can I verify DSC functionality?
intent_routes.answer: The DSC function shows the result of DSC hardware self-test performed at power-on. It will display OK if it passes, or FAIL if there is an issue requiring troubleshooting.

intent_routes.question: How do I check NMEA 2000 network status?
question_variations: Where can I find NMEA 2000 diagnostics?
What shows NMEA network health?
How to view NMEA errors?
intent_routes.answer: Select NMEA 2000 status to view: Bus State (radio network activity), TX/RX Errors (current transmission/receive errors), TX/RX Messages (total messages since power up), and Bus Load (total network loading).

intent_routes.question: What does AIS diagnostics show?
question_variations: How do I check AIS status?
Where are the AIS test results?
What information is in AIS diagnostics?
intent_routes.answer: AIS diagnostics shows: AIS-RX/TX self-test results (OK/FAIL), CH-A/B RX/TX message counts, VSWR antenna test results, and Silent Mode status (ON/OFF).

intent_routes.question: How do I change the radio's region settings?
question_variations: Where do I set the country for my radio?
How to configure regional settings?
What's the process to change radio region?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Select Reset > Region and Country 2. Choose region (EUROPE, USA/CAN or INTERNATIONAL) 3. Select your country within that region 4. Radio will restart after country selection. If your country isn't listed, select INTERNATIONAL > INTERNATIONAL.

intent_routes.question: What settings are preserved during a reset?
question_variations: Which settings don't change after reset?
What information is kept after factory reset?
What doesn't get erased in a reset?
intent_routes.answer: During reset, the following settings are preserved: MMSI/ATIS ID, AIS settings, Buddy list entries, and Custom channel names. All other settings return to factory defaults.

intent_routes.question: How do I locate a wireless handset?
question_variations: Where is my wireless handset?
How can I find my paired handset?
How to make my wireless handset beep?
intent_routes.answer: Select LOCATE A WHS from the WIRELESS HANDSET submenu, use ▲ and ▼ to select the handset, then press OK. The handset will beep for 30 seconds if it's turned on and within wireless range.
models: All models with wireless handset capability

intent_routes.question: How do I turn the wireless handset on and off?
question_variations: What's the power button for the wireless handset?
How to power up the handset?
intent_routes.answer: Long press the X key to turn the handset ON or OFF. The handset will automatically turn OFF after 90 seconds of no communication with the host radio.
references: Turning the wireless handset ON/OFF section

intent_routes.question: How do I charge the wireless handset?
question_variations: Where should I put the handset when not in use?
What's the charging method for the wireless handset?
intent_routes.answer: Place the handset in the charger cradle when not in use. It charges via the built-in contactless inductive charging system.

intent_routes.question: How do I configure wireless handset audio?
question_variations: Can I repeat audio between handset and radio?
What are the audio settings for wireless handset?
intent_routes.answer: You can select options to repeat audio between WHS and host radio. You can choose to repeat wireless handset audio on the host radio or repeat host radio audio on the wireless handset. Note that audio feedback may occur if the handset is too close to the radio's speakers.

intent_routes.question: How do I name my wireless handset?
question_variations: Can I assign a name to my handset?
How to change handset name?
intent_routes.answer: Select CONFIGURE HANDSET in the menu, use ▲ and ▼ to select the handset, press OK, enter the handset name, then press DSC/MENU to save the name.

intent_routes.question: What functions are not available on the wireless handset?
question_variations: What can't I do with the wireless handset?
Are there limitations to wireless handset functions?
intent_routes.answer: The wireless handset cannot access some SETUP functions and cannot enter HAILER mode. All other radio functions are available.

intent_routes.question: How can I check the GPS status?
question_variations: Where do I find GPS information?
How to view GPS details?
intent_routes.answer: Select GPS Status from the diagnostics menu to view fix type, SNR values, position coordinates, time, and date. Note that GPS details won't show if GPS Source is set to NMEA 2000®, NMEA 0183® or Manual.

intent_routes.question: How do I make an individual DSC call?
question_variations: How can I call a single vessel?
What are the ways to make an individual DSC call?
How do I contact another boat using DSC?
intent_routes.answer: You can make an individual DSC call in three ways: 1) MANUAL - enter the vessel's MMSI number 2) RECENT - select from recent calls list 3) CONTACTS - select from saved contacts. After selecting the vessel, use arrow keys to choose the voice communication channel.

intent_routes.question: What are the different types of distress calls available?
question_variations: What distress options can I select?
What kinds of emergency calls can I make?
List all distress call types
intent_routes.answer: The available distress call types are: Undesignated, Fire, Flooding, Collision, Grounding, Capsizing, Sinking, Adrift, Abandoning Ship, Piracy, and Man Overboard. Undesignated is the default setting.

intent_routes.question: How do I send a distress call using the DSC menu?
question_variations: What are the steps to send a distress call from the menu?
How can I make an emergency call using DSC menu?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Select DSC CALLS, then DISTRESS in the DSC Calls menu 2. Use ▲ and ▼ keys to select the nature of distress 3. Long press the Distress key and wait for the 3-second countdown before transmission
references: Send a Distress Call Section, Page 49

intent_routes.question: How do I send a distress call using the DISTRESS key?
question_variations: What's the quickest way to send a distress call?
How do I use the emergency button?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Lift the red protective cover over the Distress key 2. Short press the Distress key and use ▲ and ▼ keys to select distress type 3. Long press the Distress key and wait for 3-second countdown before transmission
references: Send a Distress Call Section, Page 49

intent_routes.question: How do I cancel a distress call?
question_variations: What should I do to stop a distress call?
Can I cancel an emergency call?
intent_routes.answer: Press the X key and then the DSC/MENU key to confirm cancellation. This sends a DISTRESS CANCEL call. You must then press the PTT key and announce the reason for the cancellation over voice.

intent_routes.question: How often can tracking retries be made?
question_variations: What is the retry limit for tracking?
How many tracking retries are allowed?
intent_routes.answer: Only one retry is made per tracking interval

intent_routes.question: What tracking intervals are available?
question_variations: How frequently can I poll buddies?
What are the position request timing options?
intent_routes.answer: Tracking intervals can be set to 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes, or 60 minutes

intent_routes.question: How many contacts can be stored?
question_variations: What is the maximum number of vessel contacts?
How many vessels can I save in contacts?
intent_routes.answer: Up to 50 vessel contacts can be stored with names and MMSI numbers

intent_routes.question: How many contact groups can be created?
question_variations: What's the group contact limit?
Maximum number of contact groups?
intent_routes.answer: Up to 20 contact groups can be created and stored in alphanumeric order

intent_routes.question: What is required to set up a group?
question_variations: How do I create a contact group?
What information is needed for group setup?
intent_routes.answer: Only a name and a Group Call ID (GCID) are required. The GCID must start with 0

intent_routes.question: What are the requirements for AIS operation?
question_variations: What do I need for AIS to work?
When will AIS function properly?
intent_routes.answer: Valid GPS data must be entered and a separate VHF antenna must be installed and connected to the AIS antenna socket

intent_routes.question: How do I make a group call on my marine radio?
question_variations: What are the ways to place a group call?
How can I contact a group of vessels?
intent_routes.answer: You can place a group call in three ways: 1) MANUAL - enter a new Group Call ID (GCID), 2) RECENT - select from recent group calls, or 3) GROUP CONTACTS - select from saved groups. After selecting, use arrow keys to choose the voice communication channel.

intent_routes.question: What is an All Ships Call used for?
question_variations: When should I use All Ships Call?
How do I broadcast to all vessels?
intent_routes.answer: All Ships Call is used to make non-Distress announcements to all DSC equipped vessels in range. It can be used for either SAFETY messages (like announcing obstacles in water) or URGENCY messages for very urgent communications.

intent_routes.question: How do I request another vessel's position?
question_variations: What are the ways to get a vessel's position?
Can I ask for another boat's location?
intent_routes.answer: You can request a vessel's position through Position Request by: 1) MANUAL - entering the vessel's MMSI number, 2) RECENT - selecting from recent calls, or 3) CONTACTS - choosing from saved contacts.

intent_routes.question: What is Track Buddy and how does it work?
question_variations: How do I track other vessels?
Can I monitor multiple boats' locations?
intent_routes.answer: Track Buddy is a feature that monitors up to 5 vessels from your CONTACTS list. It sends automatic DSC position requests at intervals you select (5, 15, 30, or 60 minutes). Received positions are displayed on the MFD.

intent_routes.question: How do I set up Track Buddy intervals?
question_variations: What tracking intervals are available?
How often can Track Buddy update positions?
intent_routes.answer: Track Buddy intervals can be set to: 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes, or 60 minutes between position requests. Select INTERVAL from the Track Buddy menu to change the frequency.

intent_routes.question: How do I see other vessels' AIS information?
question_variations: Where can I view AIS data from other boats?
How do I display AIS vessel information?
Can I see other boats on AIS?
intent_routes.answer: Other vessels with AIS transceivers will appear on the AIS plotter screen when within radio range. The details are also available on NMEA ports for display on compatible MFDs.

intent_routes.question: What needs to be done before AIS transmission works?
question_variations: How do I enable AIS transmitting?
Why isn't my AIS transmitting?
What's required for AIS transmitter setup?
intent_routes.answer: AIS static details must be completed before the AIS transmitter function can be enabled. This is done through the 'Configure Vessel' settings.

intent_routes.question: Where do I find wiring installation details?
question_variations: How do I wire the AIS unit?
What's the wiring diagram location?
Where are the installation instructions?
intent_routes.answer: Complete wiring installation details can be found in the 'Wiring diagram' section on page 83 of the manual.

intent_routes.question: How long does it take for AIS vessel details to be visible?
question_variations: When will other boats see my AIS?
What's the AIS transmission delay?
How soon is AIS data visible?
intent_routes.answer: In Class-B mode, it may take up to six minutes for your full vessel details to be visible to others.

intent_routes.question: What is Silent Mode in AIS?
question_variations: How does AIS Silent Mode work?
Can I stop AIS transmission temporarily?
Where is Silent Mode in settings?
intent_routes.answer: Silent Mode temporarily suspends AIS transmissions in Class-B mode. It can be activated through the AIS Setup menu > SILENT MODE on the radio or via a connected compatible Simrad MFD.

intent_routes.question: How do I enable silent mode on the radio?
question_variations: Where is the silent mode setting?
Can I turn on silent mode?
How to activate silent mode?
intent_routes.answer: Silent mode can be enabled through two methods: 1) Via the AIS Setup menu > SILENT MODE option on the radio, or 2) Through a connected compatible Simrad® MFD

intent_routes.question: How do I view AIS vessel information?
question_variations: Where can I see AIS data?
How to display AIS information?
Can I see AIS vessels on my radio?
intent_routes.answer: Short press the AIS/IC key to display the AIS plotter screen. The screen will show vessel names/MMSI, bearing, and distance on the left, with a PPI plot on the right showing vessel positions
references: Page 56, AIS Information and Display Section

intent_routes.question: What information is shown for AIS targets?
question_variations: What details can I see about AIS vessels?
What AIS data is displayed?
What does the AIS screen show?
intent_routes.answer: AIS target details show either vessel name or MMSI (based on display settings), bearing and distance to your position. Targets are also shown visually on a PPI plotter display
references: Page 56, AIS Information and Display Section

intent_routes.question: How do I change the AIS plotter zoom scale?
question_variations: Can I zoom the AIS display?
How to adjust AIS plotter range?
What scales are available for AIS view?
intent_routes.answer: Press the Zoom In (SCAN) or Zoom Out (TRI) keys to change the plotter scale. Available scales are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 nautical miles
references: Page 56, AIS Information and Display Section

intent_routes.question: How do I select different AIS targets on the display?
question_variations: Can I highlight AIS targets?
How to choose different AIS vessels?
How do I select AIS targets?
intent_routes.answer: Use the up and down arrow keys to highlight any AIS target shown on the plotter screen. The selected target will be indicated by a filled-in target symbol
references: Page 56, AIS Information and Display Section

intent_routes.question: How do I view full details of an AIS target?
question_variations: How can I see complete vessel information?
What's the process to view AIS target details?
How do I check vessel details in AIS?
intent_routes.answer: Press the OK/HL key when the target is highlighted to view full details including MMSI, Vessel name, distance, bearing, heading, ROT, COG, SOG, status and other vessel information.

intent_routes.question: What is the T/CPA Approach Screen?
question_variations: How does the TCPA approach mode work?
What does the T/CPA screen show?
How do I access the TCPA Approach screen?
intent_routes.answer: The T/CPA Approach Screen can be accessed by short pressing the AIS/IC key in AIS mode. It shows approaching AIS Alert target details on the left side with geographical position on the plotter PPI. The zoom range automatically adjusts to the best range for the selected target.

intent_routes.question: What units are used in AIS mode?
question_variations: Which measurement unit does AIS use?
Are different units available in AIS mode?
intent_routes.answer: Nautical Miles is the only unit used in AIS mode.

intent_routes.question: How is my vessel displayed on the plotter screen?
question_variations: What symbol represents my ship?
How do I identify my vessel on the display?
What does my vessel look like on the plotter?
intent_routes.answer: Your vessel is always shown in the center of the plotter screen, represented by a solid circle with a small protruding line indicating your bearing with respect to North.

intent_routes.question: What do other vessels look like on the plotter screen?
question_variations: How are other ships displayed?
What symbol shows other vessels?
How do I identify other boats on the display?
intent_routes.answer: Other vessels or targets are displayed as diamond shapes on the plotter screen. These targets are shown within the current zoom distance setting, with a small protruding line indicating the target's bearing. When selected, a target is shown as a solid diamond.

intent_routes.question: How do I activate the fog horn?
question_variations: How do I turn on the fog horn?
How do I start the fog horn?
What are the steps to use the fog horn?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Long press the AIS/IC key to enter IC/HAILER mode 2. Select FOG HORN and press OK 3. Scroll to select fog horn type 4. Press OK to start sounding

intent_routes.question: What types of fog horn sounds are available?
question_variations: What fog horn modes can I select?
What are the different fog horn options?
Which fog horn sounds can I use?
intent_routes.answer: There are 8 types: HORN (manual), UNDERWAY (1 long tone), STOP (2 long tones), SAIL (1 long, 2 short), ANCHOR (1 long warble), TOW (1 long, 3 short), AGROUND (warble sequence), and SIREN (manual)

intent_routes.question: How often does the automatic fog horn sound?
question_variations: What is the timing between fog horn sounds?
How frequently does the fog horn repeat?
What's the interval for fog horn signals?
intent_routes.answer: The automatic fog horn sounds approximately every 2 minutes until cancelled

intent_routes.question: How do I operate the manual HORN or SIREN?
question_variations: How does the manual horn work?
What's the process for using the HORN or SIREN mode?
How do I sound the manual horn?
intent_routes.answer: Select HORN or SIREN, then press and hold the OK key on the handset or the dedicated Horn Key. The sound will continue as long as the key is pressed

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the fog horn volume?
question_variations: Can I change the fog horn volume?
How do I make the fog horn louder or quieter?
What's the way to control fog horn volume?
intent_routes.answer: Operate the volume keys to change the volume while the fog horn is sounding

intent_routes.question: How do I use the intercom feature?
question_variations: How does the intercom mode work?
What are the steps to use intercom?
Can I talk between handsets?
intent_routes.answer: To use intercom: 1. Long press AIS/IC key and select INTERCOM 2. Select the station to talk to 3. Press PTT key to talk, release to hear reply 4. Press X key to quit. Note: Requires more than one FHS or WHS handset installed.

intent_routes.question: How do I use the hailer function?
question_variations: What are the steps for using the hailer?
How do I make announcements through the hailer?
intent_routes.answer: To use hailer: 1. Long press AIS/IC key 2. Select HAILER and press OK 3. Press PTT to talk through hailer, use volume keys to adjust volume 4. Release PTT to listen for response 5. Press X to return to normal mode. Note: Not available on wireless handset.

intent_routes.question: What is the announce mode?
question_variations: How do I make announcements to all handsets?
Can I broadcast to all units at once?
intent_routes.answer: Announce mode broadcasts to all installed handsets and speakers. To use: 1. Long press AIS/IC key and select ANNOUNCE 2. Press PTT to broadcast message 3. Press X to quit announce mode.

intent_routes.question: How do I access My Channels?
question_variations: Where can I find my favorite channels?
How do I set up channel shortcuts?
intent_routes.answer: Access My Channels by long pressing the numeric 9 key. First time shows full channel list for selection. After setup, only shows selected shortcut channels. Choose a channel to immediately switch to it.

intent_routes.question: Where are the shortcuts located?
question_variations: How do I access the shortcuts menu?
Where do I find quick access functions?
intent_routes.answer: Access Shortcuts page by long pressing the VOL/SQL selector key. Available shortcuts depend on selections made in ADD/EDIT SHORTCUTS menu.

intent_routes.question: How do I activate Man Overboard (MOB) mode?
question_variations: How do I trigger MOB?
What buttons activate Man Overboard?
How to start MOB function?
intent_routes.answer: Press and hold SCAN and TRI keys together to activate MOB mode. This will change the screen to MOB navigation mode showing distance and steering information to the MOB location.

intent_routes.question: What information is shown in MOB navigation mode?
question_variations: What does the MOB screen display?
What data can I see in MOB mode?
What navigation info appears for MOB?
intent_routes.answer: MOB navigation mode shows DST (current distance to MOB waypoint) and STEER (current bearing to MOB waypoint) with direction indicators for port turn, straight ahead, and starboard turn.

intent_routes.question: How do I access the shortcuts menu?
question_variations: Where are the shortcuts located?
How do I use radio shortcuts?
How to get to shortcut options?
intent_routes.answer: Shortcuts are accessible directly from the Shortcuts page. To edit shortcuts, long press the VOL/SQ selector key and choose from the list of available options.

intent_routes.question: What is the MY VHF page used for?
question_variations: What information does MY VHF show?
What's the purpose of MY VHF page?
Where can I find radio information?
intent_routes.answer: The MY VHF page displays radio information including MMSI number, GPS data status, Vessel Callsign, software and hardware version, and radio serial number. It's only available when enabled as a shortcut or by long pressing the VOL/SQL selector key.

intent_routes.question: How do I enter Navigation mode?
question_variations: How to activate NAV mode?
What button starts navigation mode?
How do I see navigation information?
intent_routes.answer: Long press the 6 key to enter NAV (Navigation) mode. The screen will display vessel's current SOG (Speed Over Ground) and COG (Course Over Ground). Press X/POWER key to exit.

intent_routes.question: What items come with the Blackbox?
question_variations: What's included in the Blackbox package?
What accessories come with the NRS Blackbox?
What's in the box for NRS-1 or NRS-2?
intent_routes.answer: The Blackbox comes with: NRS-1 or NRS-2 Blackbox unit, AP-1 Accessory pack with connectors, AP-2 mounting kit, AP-8 cable retainer pack, System Document pack, and a 1m power cable

intent_routes.question: What connectors are included in the AP-1 pack?
question_variations: Which connectors come in the AP-1 accessory pack?
What's in the AP-1 connector pack?
intent_routes.answer: The AP-1 pack includes 2 green 2-pin connectors for power & Hailer, one 8-pin green connector for wired speakers, one 8-pin green connector for auxiliary wiring, a wireless dipole SMA antenna, and a 10A blade-type spare fuse

intent_routes.question: What mounting hardware is provided?
question_variations: What screws come with the Blackbox?
What's included in the AP-2 mounting kit?
intent_routes.answer: The AP-2 mounting kit includes 4 stainless steel M4x25 pan-head self-tapping screws, 4 M4x25 pan-head machine screws, 4 M4 flat washers, 4 M4 split washers, and 4 M4 hex nuts

intent_routes.question: What documentation is included?
question_variations: What manuals come with the system?
What papers are included in the document pack?
intent_routes.answer: The System Document pack includes a System User Manual, Quick Start Guide, System Declaration of Conformity, and Warranty card

intent_routes.question: How many wire ties are provided?
question_variations: What's the number of wire ties included?
How many cable ties come in the package?
intent_routes.answer: 10 wire ties are included in the AP-8 Cable retainer accessory pack

intent_routes.question: What items come with the Fixed Handset?
question_variations: What's included with the HS100 handset?
What parts come in the Fixed Handset package?
What accessories are included with the Fixed Handset?
intent_routes.answer: The Fixed Handset package includes: HS100/H100 Fixed Handset, CR100 mounting cradle, mounting kit with screws and washers, 5m cable (CH100-5), cable kit with gaskets and connector, cable mounting kit, and warranty card

intent_routes.question: What mounting hardware is needed for the handset cradle?
question_variations: What screws do I need for the cradle mount?
What's in the FHS cradle mounting kit?
What size screws are used for the handset cradle?
intent_routes.answer: The cradle mounting kit (AP-3) includes: 2x M4x25 self-tapping screws, 2x M4x25 machine screws, 2x M4 flat washers, 2x M4 split washers, and 2x M4 hex nuts

intent_routes.question: What comes in the cable kit for the Fixed Handset?
question_variations: What's included in the FHS cable kit?
What parts are in accessory pack AP-4?
What components come with the handset cable?
intent_routes.answer: The FHS cable kit (AP-4) includes: bulkhead mounting plate, bulkhead mounting plate rubber gasket, cable rubber gasket, and 8-pin green connector for Handset

intent_routes.question: How long is the Fixed Handset cable?
question_variations: What length is the FHS cable?
What's the length of the handset cable?
How many meters is the CH100 cable?
intent_routes.answer: The Fixed Handset cable (CH100-5) is 5 meters long

intent_routes.question: What documentation comes with the system?
question_variations: What manuals are included?
What papers come in the document pack?
What documentation is provided?
intent_routes.answer: The System Document pack includes: System User Manual, Quick Start Guide, System Declaration of Conformity, and Warranty card

intent_routes.question: What are the mounting requirements for VHF antennas?
question_variations: How far apart should VHF antennas be mounted?
What's the required separation between VHF antennas?
Where should I mount the VHF antenna?
intent_routes.answer: VHF antennas must have adequate separation to prevent antenna cross-talk. The exact distance varies by installation and should be tested. Units must be mounted at least 50 cm (1.5 ft) from compasses and 1 m (3 ft) from other VHF antennas.

intent_routes.question: How should I prepare the mounting surface?
question_variations: What surface preparation is needed for mounting?
What should I clean before mounting?
Do I need to clean the mounting surface?
intent_routes.answer: Mount to surface areas that are clean with no dirt, old paint, or debris.

intent_routes.question: Where should I not mount the equipment?
question_variations: What are unsafe mounting locations?
Which mounting locations should I avoid?
Are there restricted mounting areas?
intent_routes.answer: Do not mount where it can be used as a hand hold, where it might be submerged, where it interferes with boat operation/launching/retrieving, or in hazardous/flammable environments.

intent_routes.question: What should I check before drilling mounting holes?
question_variations: Is it safe to drill mounting holes?
What precautions should I take before drilling?
How do I safely drill mounting holes?
intent_routes.answer: Check for hidden electrical wires or other parts behind the panel before drilling or cutting. Ensure holes will not weaken the boat's structure. Consult a qualified boat builder or marine electronics installer if unsure.

intent_routes.question: How should the Blackbox be mounted?
question_variations: What are the Blackbox mounting requirements?
Where should I install the Blackbox?
What's needed for Blackbox installation?
intent_routes.answer: Mount the Blackbox in a location that allows easy access for connecting to 12V DC power supply, antenna(s), and additional wiring.

intent_routes.question: How far should VHF antennas be separated?
question_variations: What's the minimum distance between VHF antennas?
How much space do I need between VHF antennas?
intent_routes.answer: VHF antennas must have adequate separation to prevent cross-talk. The exact distance varies by installation and should be tested. Units must be mounted at least 1 m (3 ft) away from other VHF antennas.

intent_routes.question: How far should the unit be mounted from a compass?
question_variations: What's the safe distance from a compass?
Will it affect my compass?
intent_routes.answer: Mount units at least 50 cm (1.5 ft) away from a compass to avoid creating magnetic deviation.

intent_routes.question: Where should I not mount the Blackbox?
question_variations: What are unsafe mounting locations?
Where should the Blackbox avoid being installed?
intent_routes.answer: Do not mount where it can be used as a hand hold, where it might be submerged, in hazardous/flammable environments, where it could get wet or hot (like engine compartments or near bilge), or where it will interfere with boat operations.

intent_routes.question: How should I mount the Blackbox vertically?
question_variations: What's the correct vertical mounting orientation?
Which way should the wiring face when mounting vertically?
intent_routes.answer: When mounting the Blackbox vertically, ensure the wiring glands are facing downwards to prevent water ingress.

intent_routes.question: What size drill bit do I need for the Blackbox mounting?
question_variations: What drill size for Blackbox installation?
How big should the mounting holes be for the Blackbox?
intent_routes.answer: Use a 3.0 mm (1/8") drill bit for 4.0x20 mm self-tapping screws, or 4.1 mm (3/16") drill bit for 4.0x28 machine screws.

intent_routes.question: What is the viewing angle for the CR100 handset display?
question_variations: How wide is the CR100 viewing angle?
What's the optimal viewing position for the CR100?
intent_routes.answer: The handset LCD screen has optimal horizontal and vertical viewing angles within approximately +/-20 degrees. You should be directly in front of the display or no more than 20 degrees off-center.

intent_routes.question: How long is the standard CR100 handset cable?
question_variations: What length cable comes with the CR100?
What's the standard handset extension cable length?
intent_routes.answer: The Fixed handset comes with a 5m (16.4') handset extension cable. Longer lengths are available from dealers.

intent_routes.question: How do I mount a speaker on a surface?
question_variations: What are the steps to surface mount speakers?
How do I install speakers on a wall?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Remove plastic bezels from screw holes. 2. Mark screw holes using speaker as template. 3. Drill appropriate size holes for fasteners. 4. Drill a hole for speaker wire near a corner screw hole. 5. Feed wire through mount box and surface. 6. Apply sealant around cable and screw holes. 7. Fix speaker with fasteners. 8. Ensure drain hole is at lowest side. 9. Replace plastic bezels.

intent_routes.question: How do I install a GPS-500 antenna?
question_variations: What's the process for mounting a GPS-500?
Where should I mount the GPS antenna?
intent_routes.answer: Mount externally on either pole or hard surface with clear view of sky. For pole mount: Use 1-inch 14 TPI thread pole, attach pole adapter, feed cable through, and secure with 2 screws. For surface mount: Select flat clean surface, install gasket, drill mounting holes, feed cable through, and secure with 2 screws. Run cable to Blackbox and connect to GPS connector (SMA).

intent_routes.question: Is the GPS-500 antenna required?
question_variations: Do I need to install the GPS-500?
Which models require GPS-500?
intent_routes.answer: The GPS-500 antenna is optional for NRS-1 model but mandatory for NRS-2 model.

intent_routes.question: What are the restrictions for GPS antenna placement?
question_variations: Where should I not mount the GPS antenna?
What are the GPS mounting limitations?
intent_routes.answer: Do not mount on masts where vessel motion can cause swinging and reduce accuracy. Keep at least 1 meter away from any transmitting device. Ensure clear, unobstructed view of the sky.

intent_routes.question: What are the cable installation guidelines?
question_variations: How should I run the cables?
What should I avoid when installing cables?
intent_routes.answer: Avoid sharp bends in cables, prevent water flow into connectors, keep away from radar and high current cables, avoid interference with mechanical systems, and don't run over sharp edges. Don't run data cables adjacent to transmitter or high frequency signal cables.

intent_routes.question: How do I mount the handset cable connector?
question_variations: What are the steps to install the handset connector?
How do I install the cable connector assembly?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Mark two mounting screw holes. 2. Drill holes using 2.5mm bit for self-tapping screws or 3.1mm for machine screws. 3. Cut a 24mm diameter hole centered between screw holes. 4. Attach connector cover, plate and gasket using provided screws.

intent_routes.question: What size hole do I need for the handset cable connector?
question_variations: What diameter should the connector hole be?
How big should I cut the cable connector opening?
intent_routes.answer: Cut a 24.0 mm (0.94") diameter hole for the cable connector

intent_routes.question: How do I install the BC-12 wireless handset cradle?
question_variations: What are the steps to mount the BC-12 cradle?
How do I mount the wireless handset holder?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Mark mounting screw holes. 2. Drill holes using 3.0mm bit for self-tapping screws or 4.1mm for machine screws. Cut 3.6mm hole for charger cable 54.5mm from middle. 3. Attach cradle with provided screws. 4. Connect red wire to battery+ via 2A fuse and black wire to battery-.

intent_routes.question: What power supply does the BC-12 cradle need?
question_variations: What voltage does the BC-12 cradle require?
How much power does the wireless cradle need?
intent_routes.answer: The BC-12 Wireless Handset Cradle requires a +12V DC supply for charging

intent_routes.question: What is the viewing angle for the handset display?
question_variations: How should I position the handset display?
What's the optimal viewing position for the LCD?
intent_routes.answer: The handset LCD screen has optimal horizontal and vertical viewing angles within approximately +/-20 degrees from front of display

intent_routes.question: How do I flush mount the speaker?
question_variations: What are the steps for speaker installation?
How do I install the speaker flush mounted?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Cut 98mm diameter hole in mounting surface. 2. Remove plastic bezels, fit speaker temporarily and mark screw holes. 3. Drill appropriate size holes for fasteners. 4. Fit foam gasket to rear, apply sealant to screw holes, and secure speaker.

intent_routes.question: What size hole is needed for flush mounting the speaker?
question_variations: How big should the speaker cutout be?
What diameter hole for speaker installation?
intent_routes.answer: Cut a 98 mm (3.86") diameter hole for flush mounting the speaker

intent_routes.question: How should I route cables for the Blackbox installation?
question_variations: What are the cable routing guidelines?
How do I properly run cables for the Blackbox?
What are the do's and don'ts for cable installation?
intent_routes.answer: Do: Make drip and service loops, use cable-ties to secure cables, solder/crimp and insulate connections, leave room near connectors. Don't: Make sharp bends, allow water to flow into connectors, run cables near radar/high current cables, interfere with mechanical systems, or run over sharp edges.

intent_routes.question: What size fuse is required for the Blackbox?
question_variations: What is the fuse rating?
Which fuse should I use?
intent_routes.answer: Use a 10A fuse for the Blackbox installation.

intent_routes.question: How do I access the wiring connectors on the Blackbox?
question_variations: Where are the wiring receptacles located?
How do I reach the connector terminals?
intent_routes.answer: Remove the 6 screws on the cover plate to expose the wiring connectors under the connector cover on the base unit.

intent_routes.question: What power supply does the radio require?
question_variations: What voltage does the radio need?
What are the power requirements?
intent_routes.answer: Connect the radio to a 12V DC, negative ground power supply.

intent_routes.question: How do I install the GPS antenna?
question_variations: What are the GPS antenna mounting steps?
How should I mount the GPS antenna?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Mark and drill 2 mounting holes plus cable hole. 2. Thread cable through gasket center. 3. Screw antenna to mounting surface. 4. Run GPS cable to Blackbox with any needed extensions. 5. Connect to GPS (SMA) connector on Blackbox.

intent_routes.question: What size ring terminal is required?
question_variations: What ring terminal should I use?
What's the terminal size specification?
intent_routes.answer: Ring terminal size M3, #5

intent_routes.question: What type of fuse is needed?
question_variations: What fuse specification is required?
Which fuse should I install?
intent_routes.answer: 10 A mini-blade type fuse

intent_routes.question: What GPS sources can be used with the system?

intent_routes.question: How do I set up the radio for first time use?

How do I configure the radio initially?
intent_routes.answer: Initial setup requires: 1. Select country/region (USA/CAN, EU, or INT), 2. Enter MMSI number, 3. Enter ATIS ID (EU only), 4. Enter vessel call sign, 5. Select GPS source, 6. Set time offset, 7. Choose time format, 8. Configure AIS (NRS-2 only)

intent_routes.question: What handsets can be connected?

Which handset connections are available?
intent_routes.answer: HS1 handset is mandatory, while HS2, HS3, and HS4 are optional fixed handsets that can be connected.

intent_routes.question: Can I change the MMSI number after initial setup?

Is it possible to update MMSI?
intent_routes.answer: No, MMSI entry can only be done once. Changing the MMSI requires returning the radio to a Simrad®/B&G® dealer.

intent_routes.question: How do I update the VHF radio software?

What's the process to update my VHF system?
Can I update my VHF radio firmware?
intent_routes.answer: The system software can be updated via the NMEA 2000 network using a connected Simrad/B&G MFD. Software updates for the Blackbox, Fixed Handsets, and Wireless Handsets are available in one file from the Help & Support section at www.simrad-yachting.com or www.bandg.com

intent_routes.question: What do the different power LED colors mean?
question_variations: How can I tell if my VHF radio is working properly from the LED?
What does a flashing red power LED indicate?
What does the green LED mean on my VHF?
intent_routes.answer: No LED means system is off, flashing green indicates system powering on, solid green means system is powered on and functional with GPS fix, flashing red indicates system error condition requiring diagnostic check

intent_routes.question: What do the AIS LED indicators mean?

intent_routes.question: How do I perform a factory reset?

Will a factory reset delete my MMSI?

intent_routes.question: Where can I find system diagnostic information?

Where are the diagnostic menus located?
How can I check system diagnostics?
intent_routes.answer: System diagnostics can be found on page 46, which displays System, AIS, NMEA 2000, and GPS diagnostic screens

intent_routes.question: What does AIS VSWR error mean?
question_variations: Why am I getting an AIS VSWR error?
What causes AIS VSWR error message?
How do I fix AIS VSWR error?
intent_routes.answer: AIS VSWR error indicates the AIS antenna is either missing (open circuit) or damaged (short circuit). It can also be caused by corroded wiring or connections. While you can continue operating, both transmission and reception will be affected. The recommended solution is to replace the antenna.

intent_routes.question: Why won't my VHF radio power on?
question_variations: How do I fix a radio that won't turn on?
What causes power issues with VHF radio?
Radio not powering up troubleshooting
intent_routes.answer: The radio may not power on due to: 1) Blown fuse in Blackbox, 2) Incorrect fuse/breaker size, 3) Damaged wiring, or 4) Attempting to power on from a wireless handset (must use fixed handset). Check the 10A blade fuse, reset circuit breaker, inspect wiring for damage/corrosion, and use a fixed handset power button.

intent_routes.question: How do I fix no sound from the handset?
question_variations: Why is there no audio from my handset?
Handset has no sound output
No volume from radio handset
intent_routes.answer: No sound from handset can be caused by: 1) Volume set too low - check and adjust volume settings, or 2) Handset speaker is turned OFF - turn the handset speaker ON.

intent_routes.question: Why does my system shut down when transmitting?
question_variations: Radio shuts off during transmission
VHF powers down while transmitting
What causes transmission shutdown?
intent_routes.answer: System shutdown during transmission is typically caused by insufficient power at the Blackbox power terminals or a flat battery. This is a safety feature that activates when voltage drops below specification, especially when transmitting at HI (25W) power. Check if wiring can supply required current.

intent_routes.question: Why is my GPS not working?
question_variations: How do I fix GPS issues?
No GPS fix on VHF radio
GPS problems troubleshooting
intent_routes.answer: GPS issues can be caused by: 1) Incorrect GPS Source Setting - check if set to Internal or Networked, 2) Antenna covered - ensure external GPS antenna has clear view of sky, or 3) Poor coverage in current location preventing 3D fix.

intent_routes.question: Why can I transmit but not hear anything on my VHF radio?
question_variations: Can't hear responses on VHF
Why am I not receiving any audio?
No incoming audio on VHF radio
intent_routes.answer: This typically occurs when using a Duplex channel with no repeater in range. For radio-to-radio communications, use a Simplex channel instead. To test for repeater availability, select a Duplex channel, press PTT briefly, then listen for a short burst/crack over the speaker after releasing PTT.

intent_routes.question: How do I fix poor reception on my VHF radio?
question_variations: Why is my VHF reception bad?
How to improve VHF radio reception
Static on VHF radio
intent_routes.answer: Adjust the squelch (SQL) setting so that background noise just clears. If still experiencing issues, check if power is set to LO (1W) and change to HI (25W) power by long pressing the OK key. Also verify antenna connections and test with a known good antenna if problems persist.

intent_routes.question: What causes digital noise when releasing PTT?
question_variations: Why do I hear noise after transmitting?
Digital noise after PTT release
Strange sounds after transmission
intent_routes.answer: Digital noise after PTT release can be caused by two issues: 1) ATIS function is turned ON (should only be used in European waterways), or 2) Power supply voltage is outside the optimal range of 13.6V DC ±1V DC. Turn off ATIS if not in European waters and verify proper voltage supply.
models: All VHF Radio Models with ATIS

intent_routes.question: How do I check for a failing antenna?
question_variations: Signs of bad VHF antenna
VHF antenna troubleshooting
How to test VHF antenna
intent_routes.answer: Check antenna cable for signs of corrosion due to water ingress. Inspect all antenna connections as bad connections will reduce power levels. Test performance by comparing with a known good antenna to verify functionality.

intent_routes.question: Why can't other stations hear my transmission?
question_variations: No one can hear my VHF transmission
VHF radio not transmitting properly
Others can't hear my radio
intent_routes.answer: This could be due to: 1) Power setting on LO (1W) instead of HI (25W) - change to HI power by long pressing OK key, or 2) Faulty antenna - check VHF antenna connections and test with a known good antenna.

intent_routes.question: How do I fix a failing antenna?
question_variations: What should I do if my antenna is not working?
My antenna is failing, how do I troubleshoot it?
intent_routes.answer: Check the antenna cable for signs of corrosion caused by water ingress
references: VHF Radio Help and Troubleshooting Guide

intent_routes.question: Why isn't my AIS transmitting?

How do I get AIS to start transmitting?
intent_routes.answer: AIS transmission requires: 1) Connected VHF antenna 2) Completed AIS setup details 3) Valid MMSI number 4) GPS fix 5) Silent Switch set to OFF

intent_routes.question: Why isn't DSC working?
question_variations: How do I enable DSC?
What's needed for DSC operation?
intent_routes.answer: DSC requires: 1) Valid MMSI number entered 2) DSC function turned ON 3) ATIS must be turned OFF as DSC and ATIS cannot operate simultaneously

intent_routes.question: What causes digital noise when releasing PTT?

intent_routes.answer: Digital noise after PTT release indicates ATIS function is turned ON. Only use ATIS while navigating European waterways. Turn ATIS OFF otherwise.

intent_routes.question: What are the power restrictions for on-board communications on channels 15 and 17?

What is the maximum power allowed for on-board use of channel 15?
Are there power limits for using channel 17 on board?

intent_routes.question: Where can channels 10, 67, and 73 be used for coordinated SAR operations?

Are channels 10, 67, and 73 approved for rescue operations in Canada?

intent_routes.question: What frequencies are designated for AIS channels?

intent_routes.question: Can helicopters use marine VHF frequencies?

intent_routes.question: Which channels can be used for data transmission?

Where can I transmit data on marine VHF?
Which frequencies support digital data?
intent_routes.answer: All channels except 06, 13, 15, 16, 17, 70, 75 and 76 may be used for high-speed data, facsimile transmissions, direct-printing telegraphy and data transmission, subject to special arrangement between administrations.

intent_routes.question: How can 12.5 kHz channel interleaving be implemented?

When is 12.5 kHz interleaving allowed?
Can we use 12.5 kHz channel spacing?

intent_routes.question: Can marine VHF frequencies be used on inland waterways?

intent_routes.question: What are the preferred first three frequencies for marine communication?
